1_anti_shortcut_term.loss: L = BCE + 0.5 x (1 - rho_hp) + LAMBDA x P_shuf, with BCE and rho_hp exactly v1's on the clean windows, and P_shuf = sum over the batch's training px of sigmoid(logit_shuf) / (count of the batch's training px), i.e. the mean predicted ink on the depth-permuted copies over the same px BCE averages over (the same flips and rotation, so both arms and both branches see identical pixels). The penalty's target is 0 (no ink) in BOTH arms; it never sees the teacher. Computed in fp32 from bf16-autocast logits, like the BCE.
1_anti_shortcut_term.why_0p5: [machine] On a depth-destroyed window the best a teacher-only objective can do is the teacher prior, p about 0.2457 (the pooled teacher mean on the training px, measured by this part); at LAMBDA 0.5 a student that answers that way pays 0.5 x 0.2457 = 0.1228, about 13% of v1's final loss (0.963), and its per-px gradient on the shuffled logit is LAMBDA x p(1 - p) = 0.0926, about half the typical clean BCE gradient |p - t| (the teacher sd on the training px is 0.23-0.25). So the penalty is strong enough to move the shared depth stem within a few hundred steps and weak enough that the teacher term stays the main objective. It equals the recipe's other auxiliary weight (the hp term's 0.5), so neither auxiliary outranks the other. A larger LAMBDA mostly speeds the same solution and raises the risk of suppressing the clean output; a smaller one may leave the penalty under the clipped-gradient noise (the 1.0 clip was active on nearly every v1 step). No LAMBDA was tried: there is no v2 number of any kind.
1_anti_shortcut_term.the_permuted_input: per sample, x_shuf = the SAME augmented, normalised 17 x 128 x 128 clean input x (after normalize_robust and the intensity transforms) with its 17 depth layers reordered: x_shuf[b, 0, j] = x[b, 0, perm_b[j]] for j = 0..16. Same window, same depth centre and offset, same flips and rotation, same intensity augmentation; the ONLY difference between the two inputs is depth order. Applied on the GPU by indexing, so the producer does no extra work.
1_anti_shortcut_term.permutations: a fresh uniform permutation of 0..16 per sample, from its OWN generator numpy default_rng(20261008), drawn in the producer thread right after that batch's clean draws, 8 per step in sample order; a draw equal to the identity or to the full reversal [16..0] is redrawn (the reversal is the forward-order control, held out below). [machine] 20261007 (= seed + 1) is v1's probe generator, so it is not reused. The global numpy and torch RNGs and default_rng(20261006) are never touched by it, so v2's clean stream is v1's to the byte (section 5_harness checks it). Pinned now: the first permutation is [4, 2, 14, 9, 1, 5, 13, 10, 8, 6, 12, 15, 3, 11, 16, 7, 0], the second [4, 3, 5, 12, 6, 0, 10, 9, 13, 11, 16, 15, 7, 1, 2, 14, 8]; sha1 of step 1's 8 permutations as int8 bytes f4b67288b04f, of step 2's c533edabc6c1; no redraw in the first 16 draws. Both arms draw the identical sequence.
1_anti_shortcut_term.why_the_window_layers_and_not_the_21_sla: [machine] (1) A 41-layer permutation would feed layers 0..40, reaching +-192 um + 16.2 um trilinear along the normal; v1's 3D cut of 228.0 um assumes layers 6..34 (+-134.4 um) and leaves the footprint >= 51 um from the 252405 test frame only under that assumption, so a 41-layer shuffle would break the 50 um exclusion. (2) A per-sample 21-slab permutation (the shuf21 control's construction) would need its own normalisation and intensity augmentation in the producer, which is the bottleneck (0.181 s per batch in v1) and would add RNG draws, so the two branches would differ in more than depth order. (3) Permuting the window's own 17 layers after augmentation makes the shuffled copy differ from the clean one in depth order only: whatever the student still reads from it is order-invariant content of that very window, which is the shortcut to remove. Cost, stated: the test's shuf21 windows hold 17 of the slab's 21 layers and shuf41's hold layers from the whole 41-stack, so G4 tests generalisation from this training form to those two, not the form itself.
1_anti_shortcut_term.forward_order_penalty: NOT INCLUDED. [machine] (a) Forward order is a coherent physical stack (the same sheet read from the other face), not a depth-destroyed one; penalising it teaches orientation, which the rev convention already fixes at inference. (b) With both shuffles penalised, the forward control is the one G4 control the training objective never sees, so it is the held-out witness that the penalty removed order-invariant reading rather than taught a 'looks shuffled -> 0' detector (a detector would not fire on a smooth forward stack, and its order-invariant reading would show there). (c) It would add a third forward/backward per step. Cost, stated: v1 failed fwd at 48 um (+0.0163 vs +0.0138/+0.0128); if the v2 fwd reading came from order-invariant content the shuffle penalty removes it too, and if not, G4 fails on fwd and that failure is the finding.
1_anti_shortcut_term.implementation: per micro-batch (8, or 2 x 4 under --micro 4 as v1): first v1's clean forward and backward unchanged (part = bce / npx - 0.5 x rho / nq_tot); then the permuted copy's forward under the same autocast and backward of LAMBDA x sum(sigmoid(logit_shuf) x m) / npx, gradients accumulating; then v1's single global clip at 1.0 over the summed gradient, the optimiser step and the schedule. Two sequential passes keep peak VRAM at v1's (about 1.9 GB allocated) instead of a batch of 16. The model's norms are InstanceNorm2d/3d with affine and track_running_stats False and it has no dropout (checked on CPU by this part), so no statistic couples the two branches or the samples.
1_anti_shortcut_term.logged_never_deciding: every step adds to steps.jsonl: p_shuf (P_shuf), pen = LAMBDA x P_shuf, the total loss with it, rho_hp_shuf (Pearson of hp(sigmoid(logit_shuf)) against the arm's own target over each qualifying sample's core, mean over samples with >= 2048 core px, no gradient: the scale-free witness, see limits), perm_sha1 (sha1 of that step's 8 permutations as int8), and clean_match_v1 (section 5_harness). VAL on the strip adds the permuted-input BCE, mean p and rho_hp with the fixed permutation numpy default_rng(0).permutation(17) = [2, 10, 3, 11, 0, 4, 7, 5, 16, 12, 13, 6, 9, 14, 8, 1, 15]. limits_stated_before_any_v2_number: [machine] G4's two shuffle controls are no longer independent of training: the penalty trains on depth-destroyed input of the same family, so a pass there can mean a 'looks shuffled -> no ink' detector instead of a removed shortcut. The held-out witnesses are the forward control (never penalised), the rho_hp_shuf training log, the P4 strip rows and the mirror phase nulls of G6.

[machine] P_shuf is a MAGNITUDE penalty and G4's hp r is scale-free: a student can push the mean of sigmoid(logit_shuf) toward 0 and keep its structure (sigmoid near 0 is about exp(logit), which keeps relative variation). The gradient LAMBDA x p(1 - p) shrinks as p falls, so the penalty is never driven to exact zero. rho_hp_shuf in the training log is the measure of whether structure, not only level, went; a G4 failure with a small P_shuf is that case.

[machine] the global 1.0 clip was active on nearly every v1 step, so the penalty's gradient also shrinks the clean term's effective step; v2 is v1 plus the penalty AND a slightly smaller effective clean learning rate, not v1 plus the penalty alone.
